subject: AtlasPay pilot: traffic probing & success commitments
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasPay pilot: traffic probing & success commitments

Hi Aditi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a proposal for next steps so we can lock the pilot timeline:

What we heard from AtlasPay:
- Primary workload is candidate ranking for payment reconciliation (API-based requests).
- Typical request payloads are short (70-150 tokens) but there are occasional structured-context queries up to ~850 tokens when full ledger context is included.
- Peak windows coincide with batch settlements at 02:00 and 14:00 PT; expected burst RPS could hit 450 for ~3–6 min; sustained daytime RPS target is ~35–40.
- Concurrency: 12 concurrent sessions for the reconciliation workflow; exploratory UX queries are separate and low-concurrency.

Proposed pilot goals (what success looks like):
1) Serve reconciliation traffic at 35 RPS sustained with p95 latency < 250ms for generation-only flows.
2) Handle bursts up to 450 RPS for short windows without >20% error rate or >2s tail latency.
3) Token-cost per reconciliation to be measured and compared to existing baseline; target is <= 60% of baseline cost.
4) No customer data retention beyond pilot TTL; audit log visibility for all requests.

Concrete next steps I suggest this week:
- AtlasPay to share a sanitized sample of 200 request payloads (mix of 70–150 tokens and 50 long-context examples). Attachment stub: atlaspay_sample_payloads.json.
- Redwood to provision a short-lived pilot cluster and provide a Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones and owners.
- Align on evaluation metrics and a short (2-week) soak followed by a stress window.

Ownership: I will own delivery from Redwood side; Neha will lead CS for operational acceptance; Karthik will lead the capacity/benchmark work.

Can you confirm the burst windows/times above and whether the payload mix looks representative? If you’re good, we’ll target provision on Monday (1/19) and kick off measurements Tuesday (1/20).

Thanks —
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: AtlasPay_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx (see link), atlaspay_sample_payloads.json (incoming)

Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPay pilot: traffic probing & success commitments

Hi Vivek —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few data points from our side:
- Burst windows: 01:50–02:06 PT and 13:45–14:05 PT (these are fixed settlement windows; the second can vary by ±5 minutes).
- Typical payload mix: ~78% short requests (70–150 tokens), ~20% medium (250–420 tokens), ~2% long (600–850 tokens).
- Concurrency: the reconciliation service runs across 8 workers today; realistic pilot concurrency range is 8–14.
- Error tolerance: we cannot exceed 1% silent-failure in production flows during pilot; for the trial we can accept up to 2% while we tune.

I’ve uploaded a sanitized sample set to the Drive folder (link in your MP). I’m attaching an initial CSV with RPS traces for the last 30 days — filename atlaspay_sample_payloads.json (sanitized).

We’re OK to target provisioning on 1/19. Please include a short runbook for failover to our fallback endpoint if latencies spike.

Thanks,
Aditi
Platform Engineering Lead, AtlasPay

Thanks — this looks good. A couple of operational clarifications from CS/ops before we spin up infra: 

1) Acceptance gates:
   - Functional correctness: sample set evals (we’ll run 500 deterministic replay checks) — pass rate >= 95%.
   - Latency: p95 < 250ms during steady-state; p99 < 800ms during burst windows.
   - Reliability: < 2% error rate during trial, <1% target for production.

2) Measurement plan:
   - Week 0 (provision day): smoke test + 1-hour soak at 10 RPS to validate routing and KV cache behavior.
   - Week 1 (baseline): 48-hour steady run at expected sustained RPS (35) with telemetry capture.
   - Week 2 (stress & soak): two scheduled burst windows replayed from AtlasPay traces + a 4-hour elevated-load soak to observe scaling behavior.

3) Roles & escalation:
   - Redwood ops owner: Karthik Iyer (capacity/baseline tuning).
   - CS/acceptance lead: Neha Kapoor (acceptance sign-off).
   - AtlasPay on-call: Aditi Shah (rollout approval & fallback coordination).

4) Data & compliance:
   - We will use sanitized payloads only. Any PII discovered will be redacted immediately. Redwood will not persist customer payloads beyond the pilot TTL (14 days) unless otherwise agreed.

I’ve attached a brief runbook and a checklist (AtlasPay_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx). Once Vivek confirms dates I’ll schedule the initial smoke and share the monitoring dashboard access.

Neha
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPay pilot: traffic probing & success commitments

All set from the perf side — I’ll own cluster sizing and the benchmark scripts. Quick notes:

- Initial config: 4x A100-equivalent workers with continuous batching enabled; KV cache warmed with 2,000 recent keys during smoke.
- Probing plan: I’ll run a progressive ramp (10 -> 35 -> 120 -> 250 -> 450) using AtlasPay traces and compare token-level cost and latency at each plateau.
- Metrics to capture: per-request token count, model latency, model+network p95/p99, error type tags (timeout, 5xx, model_abort).

I’ve attached the benchmark harness and a short workload deck into the Drive folder (link above). After smoke on 1/19 I’ll share an initial readout by EOD 1/20. If we observe sustained p99 > 1.5s at 250 RPS I’ll propose a short canary to test an alternate quantized model to trade cost vs tail-latency.

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
